accepted.s: On 6 February 1918, B. N. Sarma moved a resolution in the Imperial Legislative Council relating to which of the following?
accepted.x: B. N. Sarma moved the resolution for the creation of linguistic provinces in the Imperial Legislative Council on 6 February 1918.
accepted.tq: Use the date–mover–subject combination to identify the correct resolution.
accepted.sec: Resolutions on linguistic reorganisation in the Central/Imperial Legislature

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the outcome of B. N. Sarma's 1918 resolution on linguistic provinces?
o: It failed despite receiving support from some members
It was accepted only for Andhra
It was referred to the JVP Committee
It was adopted unanimously by the Imperial Legislative Council
accepted.x: The 1918 resolution for linguistic provinces failed. It nevertheless received support from K. V. Rangaswami Ayyangar and others.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a resolution receiving support from one being formally accepted.
accepted.sec: Resolutions on linguistic reorganisation in the Central/Imperial Legislature

accepted.s:
With reference to the 1918 resolution of B. N. Sarma, consider the following statements:
1. K. V. Rangaswami Ayyangar supported the resolution.
2. Muhammad Ali Jinnah opposed the resolution.
3. V. S. Srinivasa Sastri supported the resolution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: K. V. Rangaswami Ayyangar supported the resolution, while Jinnah and V. S. Srinivasa Sastri opposed it.
accepted.tq: Find the incorrectly paired supporter and opponent before selecting the coded option.
accepted.sec: Resolutions on linguistic reorganisation in the Central/Imperial Legislature

accepted.s: Who remarked, in connection with the 1918 resolution on linguistic provinces, that “the time has not come”?
accepted.x: Surendranath Banerjee stated that the time had not come for the proposed linguistic reorganisation.
accepted.tq: Test an exact quotation against the associated political figure.
accepted.sec: Resolutions on linguistic reorganisation in the Central/Imperial Legislature

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents Tej Bahadur Sapru's position on B. N. Sarma's 1918 resolution?
o: He considered the matter exclusively a provincial issue
He would support it only in respect of Andhra
He opposed linguistic provinces in every form
He supported the creation of a Kannada province only
accepted.x: Tej Bahadur Sapru indicated that he would support the proposal for Andhra only.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between general support and support restricted to Andhra.
accepted.sec: Resolutions on linguistic reorganisation in the Central/Imperial Legislature

accepted.s: B. N. Sarma formed the Andhra Rajakeeya Samiti in:
accepted.x: B. N. Sarma formed the Andhra Rajakeeya Samiti in 1917.
accepted.tq: Use the middle-year numerical options to test the exact chronology.
accepted.sec: Resolutions on linguistic reorganisation in the Central/Imperial Legislature

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Dr. Ramarao — 1925 resolution in the Council of State
2. Ramadasu Pantulu — amendment for linguistic states in 1925
3. Sankaran Nair — Tamil proposal in 1926
4. Vemavaram Ramadasu — linguistic states proposal in 1927
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Dr. Ramarao initiated the 1925 proposal, Ramadasu Pantulu amended it, Sankaran Nair moved the Tamil proposal in 1926, and Vemavaram Ramadasu moved the 1927 proposal.
accepted.tq: Verify each year–mover pair before using the comprehensive option.
accepted.sec: Resolutions on linguistic reorganisation in the Central/Imperial Legislature

accepted.s: The Andhra state proposal made by Ramadasu Pantulu in 1926 was introduced in the:
accepted.x: Ramadasu Pantulu moved the Andhra state proposal in the Council of State in 1926.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct legislative body rather than the subject of the proposal.
accepted.sec: Resolutions on linguistic reorganisation in the Central/Imperial Legislature

accepted.s: Pillalamarry Anjaneyulu moved the proposal for linguistic states in the:
accepted.x: Pillalamarry Anjaneyulu moved the proposal for linguistic states in the Madras Council.
accepted.tq: Apply the who–where association to distinguish the legislative forums.
accepted.sec: Resolutions on linguistic reorganisation in the Central/Imperial Legislature

accepted.s: Who presided over the Jaipur session of the Indian National Congress in 1948?
accepted.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided over the Jaipur session of the Indian National Congress in 1948.
accepted.tq: Match the Congress session with its presiding president.
accepted.sec: INC sessions presided by Andhras

accepted.s: Pattabhi Sitaramayya lost the 1939 Tripuri presidential contest to:
accepted.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya contested the 1939 Tripuri presidential election but lost to Subhas Chandra Bose, despite Gandhi's support for him.
accepted.tq: Use the contested election pairing rather than the later Congress presidency.
accepted.sec: INC sessions presided by Andhras

accepted.s: N. Sanjiva Reddy served as President of the Indian National Congress during:
accepted.x: N. Sanjiva Reddy served as Congress President from 1960 to 1962.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact two-year tenure from nearby chronological ranges.
accepted.sec: INC sessions presided by Andhras

accepted.s: How many Andhra delegates attended the 1886 Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress?
accepted.x: The 1886 Calcutta session had 21 Andhra delegates out of a total of 408 delegates.
accepted.tq: Test both components of a numerical ratio, not merely the delegate count.
accepted.sec: Earlier Congress stance on the Andhra province (Madras, Lucknow and Calcutta)

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT among the Andhra delegates to the 1885 Bombay session of the Indian National Congress?
accepted.x: The Andhra delegates listed for the 1885 Bombay session were P. Anandacharlu, P. Rangaiah Naidu, Nyapati Subba Rao, Gutti Kesava Pillai and Venkata Subbarayudu. Pattabhi Sitaramayya was not among them.
accepted.tq: Find the name outside the historically specified delegate group.
accepted.sec: Earlier Congress stance on the Andhra province (Madras, Lucknow and Calcutta)

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Madras session blocked the Andhra resolution
B. Lucknow session took no decision on the Andhra province
C. A separate committee was formed on the issue
D. Provincial conference refused the Andhra demand
accepted.x: The sequence was Madras in 1914, the provincial conference in 1915, Lucknow in 1916, and formation of a separate committee in 1918.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence to the four successive years 1914, 1915, 1916 and 1918.
accepted.sec: Earlier Congress stance on the Andhra province (Madras, Lucknow and Calcutta)

accepted.s: The Andhra resolution was blocked by the Tamil delegates at the Madras session of the Congress in:
accepted.x: The Andhra resolution was blocked by Tamil delegates at the 1914 Madras session.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the session year from the following provincial conference year.
accepted.sec: Earlier Congress stance on the Andhra province (Madras, Lucknow and Calcutta)

accepted.s: The Congress session held at Kakinada in 1923 was presided over by:
accepted.x: Maulana Mohammed Ali presided over the Congress session held at Kakinada in 1923.
accepted.tq: Match the Andhra venue and year with its presiding president.
accepted.sec: Congress sessions held in Andhra - town, year, president

accepted.s: Which of the following events is associated with the AICC meeting at Bezawada in 1921?
o: Presentation of Pingali Venkayya's flag design to Gandhi
accepted.x: At the 1921 AICC meeting at Bezawada, Pingali Venkayya presented his flag design to Mahatma Gandhi.
accepted.tq: Identify the distinctive event associated with a particular Congress venue.
accepted.sec: Congress sessions held in Andhra - town, year, president

accepted.s: The principal financial objective associated with the 1921 AICC meeting at Bezawada was the collection of funds for the:
accepted.x: The AICC meeting at Bezawada in 1921 was associated with the Tilak Swaraj Fund.
accepted.tq: Separate two related events at the same meeting by identifying the named fund.
accepted.sec: Congress sessions held in Andhra - town, year, president

accepted.s: The Krishna District Congress Committee, whose first meeting was held at Guntur, was formed in:
accepted.x: The Krishna District Congress Committee was formed in 1892, following the suggestions of the 1885 Congress session; its first meeting was held at Guntur.
accepted.tq: Use the exact year rather than the year of the Congress session that inspired it.
accepted.sec: Congress sessions held in Andhra - town, year, president

accepted.s: The Nehru Report of 1928 advocated linguistic provinces in accordance with the:
accepted.x: The Nehru Report advocated linguistic provinces in line with the reorganisation of Provincial Congress Committees undertaken in 1920.
accepted.tq: Link a constitutional recommendation to the earlier organisational precedent it followed.
accepted.sec: Nehru Report - stand on linguistic provinces

accepted.s: What was the significance of Jawaharlal Nehru's declaration of November 1947 regarding linguistic states?
o: He accepted only the division of the Madras Presidency
He announced the formation of Andhra State immediately
He withdrew support for linguistic reorganisation completely
He declared support for linguistic states, although immediate reorganisation was not undertaken
accepted.x: In November 1947, Nehru declared support for linguistic states, but immediate reorganisation did not follow.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a political declaration of support from immediate implementation.
accepted.sec: Post-war Congress Working Committee on linguistic provinces

accepted.s: After Independence, the Constituent Assembly retained which arrangement instead of immediately creating linguistic provinces?
o: Provinces based exclusively on revenue divisions
accepted.x: The Constituent Assembly retained the pre-Independence provinces rather than immediately implementing linguistic reorganisation.
accepted.tq: Reject options introducing criteria not associated with the post-Independence arrangement.
accepted.sec: Post-war Congress Working Committee on linguistic provinces

accepted.s: The April 1949 report of the JVP Committee primarily:
o: Rejected the demand for Andhra under all circumstances
Recommended the immediate merger of Andhra with Mysore
Postponed the creation of linguistic states
accepted.x: The JVP Committee postponed linguistic reorganisation, while allowing that Andhra could be formed if the claim to Madras city was given up.
accepted.tq: Separate postponement of a general policy from the conditional concession for Andhra.
accepted.sec: Post-war Congress Working Committee on linguistic provinces

accepted.s: According to the JVP Committee's position, Andhra could be formed only if the Andhra leaders gave up their claim to:
accepted.x: The JVP Committee stated that Andhra could be formed if the claim to Madras city was relinquished.
accepted.tq: Test the central conditionality of the Andhra recommendation.
accepted.sec: Post-war Congress Working Committee on linguistic provinces

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the immediate recommendation of the Congress Working Committee after the JVP Committee's report?
o: Formation of Andhra by merging it with Telangana
Formation of Andhra without Madras city
Complete abandonment of the Andhra demand
Formation of Andhra including Madras city
accepted.x: The Congress Working Committee recommended the formation of Andhra without Madras city.
accepted.tq: Watch for the reversed comparison between Andhra with and without Madras city.
accepted.sec: Post-war Congress Working Committee on linguistic provinces

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the JVP Committee's report:
1. It reaffirmed the general approach of the Dhar Commission.
2. It placed security, unity and economic prosperity above immediate linguistic reorganisation.
3. It stated that overwhelming public opinion could not influence democratic decision-making.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The report reaffirmed the Dhar approach and prioritised security, unity and economic prosperity. It also recognised that insistent and overwhelming public opinion would have to be respected, making statement 3 false.
accepted.tq: Identify the statement that reverses the report's qualification about democratic public opinion.
accepted.sec: Post-war Congress Working Committee on linguistic provinces

accepted.s: The Congress Working Committee report stated that, if public opinion was insistent and overwhelming, Congress leaders, as democrats, had to:
o: Suppress the demand in the national interest
Refer the matter only to the British Parliament
accepted.x: The report expressly acknowledged that democratic leaders had to submit to insistent and overwhelming public opinion.
accepted.tq: Recognise the operative conclusion in a quoted democratic principle.
accepted.sec: Post-war Congress Working Committee on linguistic provinces

accepted.s: T. T. Krishnamachari added which qualification to the proposal for creating Andhra?
o: The Andhra demand should be decided by referendum in every district
The approval of the Governor-General alone would be sufficient
The approval of neighbouring states would also be necessary
The consent of the British Cabinet would be necessary
accepted.x: T. T. Krishnamachari stated that neighbouring states would also have to consent to the creation of Andhra.
accepted.tq: Ask which authority or group was specifically associated with the additional qualification.
accepted.sec: Post-war Congress Working Committee on linguistic provinces

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to the three-member committee associated with linguistic provinces?

1. Jawaharlal Nehru — Member
2. Vallabhbhai Patel — Member
3. Pattabhi Sitaramayya — Member
4. N. Sanjiva Reddy — Member
accepted.x: The three members were Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel and Pattabhi Sitaramayya. N. Sanjiva Reddy was not a member.
accepted.tq: Use the membership-composition trap by identifying the outsider in the list.
accepted.sec: Post-war Congress Working Committee on linguistic provinces
